message.content:
Review: The problem is highly relevant to the target study: it directly tests the reported link between spatial wave coarsening and time-crystalline order while clearly distinguishing the published claim from what the supplied aggregate data can establish. The export shows changing correlation width and mean shear, but has no temporal-order measurements or run-level replication; it cannot by itself establish coarsening’s causal role. The proposed repeated-run measurements and interventions address those limitations and keep the study grounded in the 111-unit array.

Feedback: The design is thoughtful: it prespecifies observables and onset criteria, treats runs as independent units, and compares coarsening-mediated explanations with direct-drive and reverse-causality alternatives. Clarify how coupling changes coarsening without independently affecting temporal order, since that is a key causal-identification assumption. Also specify the coupling range, fitting and frequency-analysis procedures, and how thresholds and persistence windows will be selected relative to drive cycles and finite-record effects. The drive-only and disorder controls are useful, though the disorder condition is appropriately framed as conditional. Claims about relevance to other mechanical systems should remain prospective until broader tests support them.

Rating (1-5): 4
